title: Meaning Before Naming: A Readout-Retention Architecture of Affective-Semantic Reorganization (Standalone Concept Note v1.0 FULL)

equations.label: MBN-readout
equations.meaning: A bounded readout: what becomes accessible to reader R_H from a finite externally available pattern x_n under current organization H_n and context c_n — not a copy of the source event.

equations.label: MBN-config
equations.meaning: A context-sensitive affective-semantic configuration, written schematically as a function of the readout, retained memory M, affective weighting A, currently available linguistic/conceptual organization L, and value/action relevance V; the notation is architectural, not a claim about literal neural variables.

equations.label: MBN-experience
equations.meaning: Lived experience represented at a higher descriptive level, with B_n marking embodiment; inherits the level separation in Human LoRA that the lived event cannot be identified with a parameter update or a bare signal.

equations.label: MBN-retention
equations.text: H_{n+1} = U(H_n, Retain(E_n, r_n, μ_n), δ^world_{n:n+1})
equations.meaning: Only some residue is retained: the reader's organization updates via U from prior organization, a Retain operator over experience/readout/configuration, and later correction or resistance δ^world; an intense moment may produce little durable change while a quieter event may reorganize later interpretation.

equations.label: MBN-naming
equations.meaning: Explicit naming is optional and temporally placed after the readout event: ℓ_n is a linguistic articulation, label, metaphor, description, or question generated from E_n and μ_n — the formal sense in which meaning may precede naming (E_n, μ_n before ℓ_n).

equations.label: MBN-resonance-diagnostic
equations.meaning: A finite diagnostic for resonance: the change in a task- or experience-relative accessibility profile A_H before and after an encounter; a positive change in one region does not imply global improvement, only that some relation/memory/possibility became more accessible under the declared reader. (This original resonance definition is noted elsewhere in the programme as later superseded by Experience v2's external–internal congruence definition.)

equations.label: MBN-articulation
equations.section: 7. Language Is a Special Transport Layer, Not the Container of Meaning
equations.meaning: A human state Z_{H,t} is articulated through language L_H as a bounded question or expression Q_{H,t}; Q_{H,t} is not identical to the whole state — articulation exports only part of what is retained and available.

equations.label: §8-non-collapse-chain
equations.section: 8. From Felt Change to Retained Human Change
equations.meaning: The architecture separates exposure to a pattern, the intensity with which it is felt, whether it is retained, and whether retention constitutes improvement — these four are not interchangeable.

equations.label: §11-non-collapse-laws
equations.text: external pattern ≠ meaning; meaning ≠ explicit naming; shared stimulus ≠ shared inner state; affective intensity ≠ epistemic warrant; accessibility ≠ truth; resonance ≠ understanding; retention ≠ benefit; verbalization ≠ lossless translation; same surface form ≠ same reader-relative meaning
equations.meaning: The nine load-bearing non-collapse distinctions of the extension, keeping affective-semantic reorganization revisable rather than allowing intensity, familiarity, or repetition to become self-certifying.

equations.label: H1
equations.meaning: For at least some classes of experience, task-relevant changes in affective or relational accessibility will be detectable before stable explicit naming.

equations.label: H2
equations.meaning: The same external pattern will produce systematically different readout profiles as reader history, context, or prior organization changes, even when the source pattern is held fixed.

equations.label: H3
equations.meaning: Later verbal description will fail to preserve some distinctions present in immediate experience, while also adding distinctions that were not previously explicit.

equations.label: H4
equations.meaning: Immediate intensity will not perfectly predict delayed retained reorganization.

equations.label: H5
equations.meaning: Naming after an initially difficult-to-articulate experience will sometimes reorganize subsequent readout of the same or related patterns rather than merely describe a fixed prior state.

equations.label: H6
equations.meaning: Even when H1–H5 are supported, no inference to truth, wisdom, well-being, or ethical value follows without independent criteria.
